intent: New themed map layouts; reference supplies camera, tile scale, portal family and restrained non-pixel rendering.

prompts.name: 지하 감옥
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a complete landscape tactical tower-defense battle map for the original dungeon-exploration game Dungeon Expedition.
Input image role: STYLE, CAMERA, TILE SCALE and PHYSICAL PORTAL DESIGN REFERENCE ONLY. Make a NEW map layout, not a recolor of this reference.
Style: polished non-pixel anime-fantasy tactical environment, quiet matte painted planes, restrained soft 3D shading, clean anti-aliased forms. Broad stone surfaces with very few cracks, no fine rubble, no dense texture, no ornamental clutter. Match the restrained reference finish. No photorealism, pixel art, glossy toy look or miniature diorama.
Camera: fixed high oblique tactical view like the reference, tile rows run horizontally, columns run vertically/slightly away from camera. Never rotate the board into a 45-degree diamond. Wide landscape composition, ideally 1536 x 1024.
Playability: one large contiguous roughly 15-column by 10-row uniform square-cell board. Clear regular cell boundaries on ground and on raised platforms, all tile footprints on the SAME lattice. Two physical terrain heights only: walkable low stone floor for melee placement and low flat-topped raised stone platforms for ranged/healer placement. Raised tops must be EMPTY, broad and deployable, roughly 25-35 usable elevated cells in separated groups; keep many ground-placement cells and wide connected lanes. Show only a short consistent front face on each raised platform. No floating platforms, overlapping floors or roofs hiding paths.
Enemy routes are connected winding rectilinear corridors with several right-angle turns and at least two branches; no straight corridor from entrance to goal. Clearly distinguish flat deployable high ground from dark impassable wall blocks or water/lava hazards. Leave generous empty tile space for SD characters and combat effects.
Portal rules: exactly TWO physical BLUE-lit stone archway doors are defense goals. Put both on accessible path tiles, with clear visible landing space. Use THREE physical RED-lit stone entrance arches for enemies, positioned along the opposite perimeter. Doors must sit on the board and connect to the paths. Use the same restrained medieval stone portal family as the reference. No wireframe cubes, box markers, icons or painted arrows.
Framing: the playable board dominates and is entirely visible; only a narrow surrounding wall/void border. Keep decorations at the perimeter or inside blocked footprints, not scattered over deployable squares.
No characters, monsters, UI, portraits, text, labels, numbers, logos, watermark, grid coordinate labels or route arrows. Opaque finished game background.
Theme and NEW layout: a slate-gray subterranean prison cellblock, iron-barred cells along the upper and lower perimeter, a few large square columns and restrained amber wall lanterns. The route structure is a BROAD DOUBLE-SERPENTINE: enemy arches at upper-left, middle-left and lower-left feed two long staggered S-shaped lanes that cross through a wide central junction, then split to the two blue goal doors near upper-right and lower-right. Four offset rectangular high-ground islands form the bends, with extra small 1x2 high-ground positions near the central junction. Large empty clean stone corridors take priority over cages and props. A small number of dark partition walls create readable right-angle detours. Cool desaturated gray stone, charcoal iron, burgundy banners only on the outer walls. No torture props, bodies or gore.

Theme and NEW layout: a black-basalt dungeon chamber around a sealed boss altar, with a few contained orange lava basins. STRUCTURE: a large solid 3x3 central sealed altar block splits the floor into TWO ASYMMETRIC U-SHAPED FLANK ROUTES. Three red entrance arches at upper-left, middle-left and lower-left feed long angular detours around the altar, then reach the two blue goal doors at upper-right and lower-right. A short central connector near the rear gives a tactical junction; neither lane should be a straight shot. Wide low-ground landing tiles support melee blocking. Lava is restricted to blocked side basins and one narrow rear fissure, not painted across the usable tile floors. Limit bright lava to a small fraction of the image; dark charcoal stone planes, muted iron-red architecture, restrained warm accents, no excessive fire, smoke or lava particles, no giant statue, no monster.
